goal: Get FunClip's command-line demo (README section C) working on CPU: download the example video from the README's URL, run `python funclip/videoclipper.py --stage 1 --file <video> --output_dir <dir>` to produce the recognition result and <dir>/total.srt, then run `--stage 2` on the same video and output dir with --dest_text set to a sentence copied from that recognition result, --start_ost 0 --end_ost 100 --output_file <dir>/res.mp4, to produce a clipped video and its SRT.
check: The hidden test runs stage 1 on the README example video, takes a sentence from total.srt as --dest_text, runs stage 2, and checks that a short clipped mp4 and its SRT with Chinese text were written.

revision.by: fairness review (every maintained-set exam re-checked against the source)
issues: The oracle downloads with wget, which is not in the base image, so it died at line 7 before testing anything. This is an oracle defect, even though the README also uses wget.

The README's literal --dest_text is not spoken in the README's example video. The audit re-run got 'No period found' in stage 2, and the probe's NOTES found the sentence only in 2022云栖大会_片段2.mp4. A fixed stage-2 sentence therefore makes the test hinge on a mismatched README asset rather than on clipping. v2 takes the sentence from the stage-1 total.srt, which is the documented workflow.

Stage 2 with --output_dir always writes <name>_no{N}.mp4, so --output_file ./output/res.mp4 yields res_no0.mp4. v2 accepts either name: the README pins the name, but the suffix is cosmetic and not the core clipping function.
Separately, stage 2 at this commit crashes as soon as any match is found: VideoClipper(None) never sets .lang, and video_clip reads self.lang. This is a repo bug, which the probe also patched.
